Micro Cooling Concepts, Inc. has developed a turbine blade cooling concept that provides enhanced internal impingement cooling effectiveness via the use of microstructured impingement surfaces.
The microtextured surfaces significantly increase the cooling capability of the impinging flow, as compared to a conventional untextured surface.
The cooling approach can be combined with microchannel cooling and external film cooling to tailor the cooling capability per the external heating profile.
The cooling system can be optimized to minimize impact on engine performance.
In a modern gas turbine engine, the combustor outlet temperatures can exceed the blade and disk material limits by 600°F or more.
Internal convective cooling is inadequate in many blade locations, and both internal and film cooling approaches can lead to significant performance penalties in the engine.
The cooling technology can benefit turbine engine development for military and commercial aircraft, power generation plants, electronics, industrial processes, automotive, and lasers.
The Versatile Affordable Advanced Turbine Engine (VAATE) initiative aims to enable higher combustion temperatures with lower engine penalties.
The paper mentions evaluating the suitability of high-temperature materials such as those from the Inconel or HAYNES series for this turbine blade cooling application.
Micro Cooling Concepts, Inc. is located in Huntington Beach, California.
